name: al-Layth ibn Sa'd
nameAr: الليث بن سعد بن عبد الرحمن الفهمي، أبو الحارث المصري

nisbas.en: al-Fahmi (by clientage to Fahm, of Qays Aylan)

mawla: Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir al-Fahmi (or, some said, of Thabit ibn Za'in, his grandfather); his family claimed Persian descent from Isfahan, which Ibn Yunus found unfounded
bornNote: 94 (Ibn Bukayr and others; Ibn Sa'd: 93 or 94, in the caliphate of al-Walid); Ibn Abi Maryam: 93; some said 92. Born at Qarqashandah, a village about four parasangs from Fustat.
diedNote: Sha'ban 175 (Taqrib); Ibn Sa'd: Friday, with fourteen nights of Sha'ban remaining, 175, in the caliphate of al-Mahdi.

deathVariants.source: Tahdhib al-Kamal 24/261 (editor's note from al-Tabaqat 7/517); Taqrib 5684

taqrib.en: Reliable and firm, a jurist and a renowned imam.

role: Jurist and mufti of Egypt in his time

students.name: Isa ibn Hammad Zughbah, the last reliable narrator from him
Abu Salih Abdullah ibn Salih, his scribe
students.nameAr: عبد الله بن صالح كاتب الليث

verdicts.ar: الليث بن سعد كثير العلم صحيح الحديث
verdicts.en: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd: much knowledge, sound hadith.

verdicts.ar: ما في هؤلاء المصريين أثبت من الليث بن سعد، لا عمرو بن الحارث ولا أحد
verdicts.en: Among these Egyptians none is firmer than al-Layth ibn Sa'd, not Amr ibn al-Harith nor anyone.

verdicts.via: Abu Dawud, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn
verdicts.ar: الليث ثقة، ولكن في أخذه سهولة
verdicts.en: Al-Layth is reliable, but there was laxity in how he took hadith.

verdicts.via: Ishaq ibn Mansur; Ibn Abi Khaythamah

verdicts.ar: صدوق. قلت: يحتج بحديثه؟ قال: إي لعمري
verdicts.en: Truthful. "Is his hadith used as proof?" "Yes, by my life."

verdicts.ar: كان قد استقل بالفتوى في زمانه، وكان ثقة كثير الحديث صحيحه، وكان سريا من الرجال نبيلا سخيا
verdicts.en: He alone carried the giving of legal opinions in his time; he was reliable, prolific, sound in hadith, a man of standing, noble and generous.

verdicts.ar: الليث ثقة، وهو دونهم في الزهري، يعني دون مالك ومعمر وابن عيينة، وفي حديثه عن الزهري بعض الاضطراب
verdicts.en: Al-Layth is reliable, but below them in al-Zuhri, that is below Malik, Ma'mar and Ibn Uyaynah, and his hadith from al-Zuhri has some inconsistency.

verdicts.ar: الليث أفقه من مالك إلا أن أصحابه لم يقوموا به
verdicts.en: Al-Layth is a greater jurist than Malik, except that his followers did not carry his work forward.
verdicts.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 3/481; the same judgement from Yahya ibn Bukayr in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 7/179 ("but the fortune was Malik's")

verdicts.en: He was the imam of his age, undisputed.
Reliable and firm, a jurist and a renowned imam.

dhahabi.ar: ثبت من نظراء مالك، قيل: كان مغله في العام ثمانين ألف دينار فما وجبت عليه زكاة
dhahabi.en: Firm, a peer of Malik; it is said his yearly income was eighty thousand dinars and zakat never fell due on him.

flags.label: Laxity in taking hadith; al-Zuhri material
flags.detail: Ahmad: "reliable, but there was laxity in how he took"; Ya'qub ibn Shaybah: below Malik, Ma'mar and Ibn Uyaynah in al-Zuhri with some inconsistency; al-Fallas: his hearing from al-Zuhri was by reading (qira'ah). None of this touches his hadith from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, whom he called "our master and our scholar".

bio: The imam of Egypt in the second century, a peer of Malik in rank and, in al-Shafi'i's judgement, his superior in jurisprudence though without followers to carry his school on. Born in 94 at Qarqashandah, he travelled to Makkah and Madinah in 113 and heard Ata', Nafi' and al-Zuhri, carried the fatwa of Egypt alone in his generation, and was famous for immense wealth given away as fast as it came: when Malik sent him a gift of Madinan produce he sent back a thousand dinars (al-Nawawi, from Qutaybah). Yazid ibn Abi Habib was his teacher and his link to the earlier Egyptian school; Qutaybah, Amr ibn Khalid and Ibn Rumh carried his hadith to the compilers. He died in Sha'ban 175.
